uncited: This family encompasses optimization strategies for reconstructing 3D Gaussian primitives from 2D images, focusing on how the scene representation is learned and trained.
It addresses the problem of parameter optimization (positions, covariances, opacities, colors) via differentiable rendering.

It is distinguished from sibling methods like [Splatting Without the Blur](1157-splatting-without-the-blur.md) by its reliance on gradient-based learning rather than purely analytical or heuristic initialization, and from [Rendering Pipelines and Passes](1411-rendering-pipelines-and-passes.md) by its focus on the training loop rather than the inference rasterization.

Loss functions typically combine photometric reconstruction error, such as $\mathcal{L}_{L1}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{MSE}$, with perceptual or structural metrics like $\mathcal{L}_{MS-SSIM}$ or $\mathcal{L}_{LPIPS}$ [6136-instantsplat.md][6464-pixelsplat.md].
